subject: FFWT-HAC-CVCD
definition: Experimental multiscale signal branch combining fractal-weighted transforms, hierarchical analysis, and controlled compression/decompression under OAK benchmarking.

claims.text: A task-specific FFWT representation may improve anomaly detection for some multiscale non-stationary signals when compared under matched protocols.
claims.canonical_key: ffwt improves anomaly detection under matched protocols
assumptions: baselines are tuned with the same validation budget
failure_conditions: FFWT fails to improve AUROC or localization error across preregistered datasets and seeds
observed gains disappear under ablation or matched hyperparameter search

claims.text: Naive fractal weighting does not generally outperform an unweighted Haar transform for sparse reconstruction at the same coefficient retention fraction.
claims.canonical_key: naive fractal weighting improves sparse reconstruction
assumptions: the recorded synthetic benchmark and metric are reproduced
failure_conditions: a fair reproduced benchmark shows consistent lower reconstruction error for the naive weighting

evidence.title: Naive fractal weighting lost to Haar FWT on synthetic reconstruction

metadata.interpretation: task-specific negative result, not universal refutation

evidence.title: M-minus rule: fractal weighting is not automatically superior

reusable_rules: separate reconstruction utility from anomaly utility

transitions.cause: Transform family and OAK benchmark path were documented.
residues: formal equations and external baselines incomplete

transitions.cause: Exact Haar reconstruction and compressed synthetic benchmark were executed.
Naive fractal weighting failed to beat the Haar baseline on the recorded reconstruction task.
residues: negative result applies to one task and one heuristic

transitions.cause: The universal superiority claim was narrowed to anomaly, denoising, and classification tasks requiring new baselines.
residues: real Raman and FTIR datasets missing

next_actions: Run anomaly benchmarks against DWT and scattering transforms with identical seeds and tuning budgets.
Add real Raman or FTIR datasets with provenance and train-test isolation.
Measure runtime, memory, robustness, and localization error in addition to reconstruction error.

metadata.oak_boundary: The anomaly-detection claim remains unverified until matched external baselines and datasets are run.
